object.description: A long-necked turtle painted in the X-ray style of western Arnhem Land, with its backbone and organs drawn inside the outline. The X-ray convention appears in Kakadu's galleries over the last two or three thousand years, at the end of a painting tradition that goes back more than 20,000 years, and shows the food animals of the wetlands: barramundi, catfish, goannas, wallabies and turtles.
facts: Kakadu's rock art tradition is one of the longest continuous ones in the world, and the Bininj and Mungguy custodians still know the stories behind many paintings.
X-ray paintings show what you learn by butchering the animal: which parts are eaten and how.
Kakadu was listed as a World Heritage Site in 1981 for both its nature and its culture.
